title: Topics that forget, topics that remember
goal: The log is storage with a policy, and right now every policy is a default. Decide how long payment events live, then give the balance read model a compacted topic — latest value per key — so step 13's rebuild starts from a snapshot instead of replaying history.
startWith: Step 13 finished: balance-service projecting events into a read model it can rebuild.

newIdeas.plain: How long a topic keeps events before deleting them — a week, by default, chosen by nobody. Your replay window and your audit trail end exactly here, so it is a business decision wearing a config key.
cleanup.policy=compact keeps the newest record per key instead of deleting by age. The topic becomes a table shaped like a log: consume it from the start and you hold the latest state of every key.
A record with a key and a null value. On a compacted topic it means delete this key — how a closed wallet eventually disappears from the snapshot.
The cleaner runs when it runs — recent duplicates survive until it does. Consumers of a compacted topic still see repeats, so step 11's rule still applies: every consumer is idempotent, always.

tasks.why: The first time retention matters is the day you need an event that expired. That day is a bad day to learn the default was seven days.
tasks.how: Read what the events topic has now, then set it to what the ledger actually needs — 30 days here, and write down why in the runbook. The outbox table from step 10 remains the system of record; the topic is transport, not archive.

blocks.label: Read, then set
blocks.body:
docker exec -it lf-redpanda rpk topic describe ledgerflow.ledger.wallet-hold.events.v1
docker exec -it lf-redpanda rpk topic alter-config \
  ledgerflow.ledger.wallet-hold.events.v1 --set retention.ms=2592000000   # 30 days

check.run: docker exec -it lf-redpanda rpk topic describe ledgerflow.ledger.wallet-hold.events.v1
check.expect: retention.ms shows 2592000000, and you can say out loud why it is 30 days.

tasks.why: Rebuilding balance-service by replaying every event ever gets slower every week, forever. A compacted topic of latest balances is a rebuild that costs the same next year as today.
tasks.how: One topic, keyed by wallet id, compacted. In dev, force small segments so the cleaner actually runs while you watch — production would never set segment.ms this low.

blocks.label: Create it
blocks.body:
docker exec -it lf-redpanda rpk topic create ledgerflow.balance.snapshots.v1 \
  -p 6 \
  -c cleanup.policy=compact \
  -c segment.ms=10000            # dev only: make the cleaner visible

blocks.label: balance: publish the snapshot after each apply

tasks.why: Compaction is invisible until you catch it in the act, and an invisible mechanism is one you will not trust when it matters.
tasks.how: Move one wallet's balance a dozen times, wait out the segment roll, then consume the snapshot topic from the start. You should get the latest value per key plus a short uncompacted tail — not twelve records.

blocks.label: Consume from the beginning
blocks.body:
docker exec -it lf-redpanda rpk topic consume \
  ledgerflow.balance.snapshots.v1 -o start -f 'key=%k  %v\n'

check.run: docker exec -it lf-redpanda rpk topic consume ledgerflow.balance.snapshots.v1 -o start -f '%k\n' | sort | uniq -c
check.expect: Each wallet appears once or twice, not once per update.

tasks.do: Rebuild the read model from the snapshot
tasks.why: This is the payoff: delete the read model, restore it from the compacted topic plus the recent event tail, and the rebuild time no longer grows with history.
tasks.how: Wipe balance-service's store, consume snapshots from the start to seed it, then resume the normal event subscription from the projection's last recorded position. Time it, and note the number next to the full-replay time from step 13.

blocks.label: The order matters
blocks.body: Seed from snapshots first, then apply the event tail. The snapshot carries a version per wallet, so tail events at or below it are skipped by the same idempotency check step 11 forced on you — the two mechanisms compose instead of fighting.

proof.run: docker exec -it lf-redpanda rpk topic consume ledgerflow.balance.snapshots.v1 -o start -f '%k\n' | sort | uniq -c
proof.expect: One latest record per wallet (plus a short tail), and a rebuilt balance-service that agrees with the ledger.
proof.note: If every update is still there, the cleaner has not run — check segment.ms and give it a minute.

doneWhen: You can state, for every topic, how long it keeps data and why — and the balance model rebuilds from a compacted snapshot instead of replaying all of history.

lessons.title: The Terminal tool window splits
lessons.teach: This step is one long rpk conversation. Open the IDE terminal (Alt+F12) and split it: producer loop on one side, rpk topic consume watching compaction on the other, code above both. Watching the cleaner work while you publish is the whole lesson.
lessons.fallbackTip: tmux, or two terminal windows side by side.
